content: Acamprosate is a medication used in conjunction with counseling and social support to assist individuals who have stopped consuming large amounts of alcohol in maintaining abstinence. Chronic alcohol consumption alters brain function, and acamprosate helps restore normal brain activity in individuals who have consumed excessive alcohol. However, it does not prevent withdrawal symptoms that may occur when alcohol consumption is stopped. Acamprosate is not effective in individuals who have not ceased drinking alcohol or those who continue to consume large amounts of alcohol while also misusing other substances, such as illicit drugs or prescription medications. Acamprosate is available as a delayed-release tablet to be taken orally, typically three times a day, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to take the medication at the same times each day, such as with breakfast, lunch, and dinner. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dosage or frequency. Swallow the tablets whole; do not split, chew, or crush them. Acamprosate is effective in preventing alcohol consumption only while you are actively taking it. Continue taking the medication even if you feel confident that you will not resume drinking. Do not discontinue use without consulting your doctor. If you consume alcohol while taking acamprosate, continue the medication and contact your doctor. Acamprosate does not cause adverse reactions if alcohol is consumed during treatment. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking acamprosate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to acamprosate, any other medications, or sulfites. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, particularly antidepressants. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication dosages or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have ever had thoughts of self-harm or suicide, attempted suicide, or misused substances such as street drugs or prescription medications. Additionally, disclose any history of depression or kidney disease. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking acamprosate, contact your doctor. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform the healthcare provider that you are taking acamprosate. Be aware that acamprosate may affect your thinking, decision-making abilities, and coordination. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you understand how the medication affects you. Note that individuals who consume large amounts of alcohol are often at risk of depression and may attempt self-harm or suicide. Acamprosate does not reduce this risk and may increase it. Depression may develop even if you do not resume drinking. You or your family should contact your doctor immediately if you experience symptoms of depression, such as sadness, anxiety, hopelessness, guilt, worthlessness, helplessness, loss of interest in activities, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, sleep disturbances, appetite or weight changes, restlessness, or thoughts of self-harm or suicide. Ensure your family is aware of these symptoms so they can seek medical attention on your behalf if necessary. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking acamprosate. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Acamprosate may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: diarrhea, gas, upset stomach, loss of appetite, dry mouth, dizziness, itching, or weakness. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. Contact your doctor if you experience burning, tingling, or numbness in your extremities, or a rash. Report any unusual problems while taking this medication to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store acamprosate in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include diarrhea. Prolonged excessive use of acamprosate may lead to symptoms such as loss of appetite, upset stomach, constipation, extreme thirst, fatigue, muscle weakness, restlessness, or confusion. Contact your doctor if you experience any of these symptoms. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any counselors or support groups. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
